slides.headline: Six-point type on the back of a jar, //[[gold]]in a dim shop[[/gold]]
slides.sub: You're holding it at arm's length. It isn't helping.

slides.headline: Photo, pinch, zoom, squint, give up
slides.body: Or you put the jar back and buy the one you already know, which is how you've eaten the same four things for a year.

slides.headline: You hold it up and it [[gold]]reads it to you[[/gold]]
slides.body: Ingredients, allergen line, the serving size the numbers are actually based on. Out loud, while the jar is still in your hand.

turns.text: Is there anything in this I shouldn't have?
It lists milk powder, third ingredient. You told me dairy was out — I'd put this one back.

slides.headline: You only tell it once
slides.body: Say the allergy a single time and it's there in every session afterwards — next week, next shop, without you raising it again.

items.text: Washing instructions on a clothing tag
items.note: the ones printed in grey on grey

items.text: A handwritten note someone left you
Cooking instructions on a packet across the kitchen
A form, a sign, a screen, a receipt

slides.headline: Next unreadable thing, just ask
slides.body: Free on iPhone. No account, no password, and you can delete everything in one tap.

caption.tiktok:
Nutrition labels are printed for ants and shops are lit like caves. Hold the phone up, ask what's in it, and it reads the thing to you — including whether it's got the one ingredient you can't have, because you only have to tell it that once.

Free on iPhone — search “My Argus” on the App Store (the gold ring).
